messages:
jessica: FYI ACME just pinged — spike in 429s + unexpected billing after we pushed the EU limit change ~08:15 UTC. They see AUTH failures for some keys. example req id: req_8ab12f.
kevin: Do we have response headers or a sample curl? need to know if this is quota enforcement or auth mapping.
jessica: paste (scrubbed):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-reset: 1690001234
x-rate-limit-policy: new-eu-small
x-auth-error: token_not_found
```
Also CS says billing for ACME jumped ~40% in the last hour.
sasha: quick look at infra logs: looks like a key->plan mapping mismatch during the policy merge. some keys fell back to the smaller tier while meter started counting differently.
deploy-bot: rollout 'rate-policy-eu-small' finished at 2026-03-16T08:14:21Z (canary 20% -> 100%).
carla: Can we pause and revert the EU rollout? if it's a mapping race we should stop traffic and rollback to previous policy while we triage.
kevin: Agreed. Proposed steps: pause rollout, apply previous policy config id=policy-2026-02-10-v1, and whitelist impacted keys. Commands:
```
redwoodctl rollout pause --region eu && 
redwoodctl policy apply --id policy-2026-02-10-v1
```
I'll also open the rollback.
jessica: Impacted customers (reported): acme-inc, payinfra, internal-integration-3. CS wants an ETA to restore.
sasha: I'll grep for mapping errors and run the key-fix script: `scripts/fix_key_mapping.sh policy-2026-03-16` — if duplicate rule ordering caused fallback we can patch mapping quickly.
kevin: Also create a billing ticket to reverse anomalous charges asap (billing@redwood). will cc @carla. for immediate relief we can whitelist ACME's key: `redwoodctl whitelist-key --key acme-prod-xxx --region eu`
carla: doing the rollback + whitelist now. monitoring token-lookup-errors and 429_rate for next 10m.
jessica: letting ACME know we paused the rollout and whitelisted their key, will ask them to confirm. :thumbsup:
sasha: root cause found — policy merge resulted in duplicate rules so some keys matched the smaller plan rule first. PR with fix ready, will re-run canary with corrected ordering.
kevin: For follow-up: keep canary at 10% for 30m next time, add an explicit key-mapping-stable metric to gate automated ramp, and add a rollback playbook link to the deploy pipeline.
jessica: ACME confirms errors dropped to zero after whitelist + rollback. closing the immediate customer escalations, we'll run a brief postmortem and circle back to CS.
